title: Observations of highly inclined disks with ALMA: Results from <SUP>12</SUP>CO gas and continuum observations
question: Study the radial and vertical extents of 12CO gas, millimeter dust continuum, and optical/NIR scattered light in 14 highly inclined protoplanetary disks to constrain radial drift and vertical settling, and estimate dynamical stellar masses.

data.bands: Band 7 (~0.88 mm / 868 µm) for 13 sources; Band 6 (1300 µm) for Oph 163131

recipe.method: Generate moment 0 and moment 1 maps from the 12CO image cubes using bettermoments with 3-sigma clipping.

recipe.goal: Measure disk position angles and continuum/12CO fluxes
recipe.method: Manually measure orientation of major axes for PA. Integrate continuum flux and moment 0 12CO line flux within rectangular apertures tailored to each disk.
key_parameters: 10% flux calibration uncertainty combined quadratically with measurement error

recipe.goal: Measure ALMA continuum and 12CO radial extents
recipe.method: Extract surface brightness profiles along the major axis integrated over the vertical extent and normalized by peak intensity. For 12CO, visually select the channel with maximum radial extent on blue and red sides in the image cube. Measure diameter at 3-sigma above background noise.
key_parameters: 3-sigma threshold above background (5-sigma minimum between disks on West side of HH 48 NE)

recipe.goal: Measure ALMA continuum and 12CO vertical extents and disk inclinations
recipe.method: Extract minor-axis brightness profiles. For continuum, fit a Gaussian to obtain FWHM and quadratically subtract beam FWHM. Estimate inclination from axis ratio using major axis size at 50% peak flux (or ellipse fit to ring for Lup 160708). For 12CO, collapse all channels with detected emission and measure minor-axis extent at 3-sigma without Gaussian fitting.
key_parameters: 50% maximum flux for continuum axis ratio; 3-sigma threshold for 12CO vertical extent

recipe.goal: Estimate dynamical stellar masses and systemic velocities from PV diagrams
recipe.method: Construct position-velocity (PV) diagrams and superimpose 3 Keplerian velocity curves (fitting outermost maximum intensity for lower limit, signal-to-noise transition for preferred mass, and off-signal for upper limit) while visually aligning systemic velocity symmetrically.
assumptions: Keplerian rotation; distances of 130 pc (Taurus), 140 pc (Ophiuchus, Upper-Scorpius), 160 pc (Lupus), 190 pc (Chamaeleon) from Zucker et al. (2020); inclinations from literature or midpoint between continuum axis-ratio lower limit and 90 deg.

recipe.goal: Measure optical/NIR scattered light radial and vertical extents and perform statistical comparisons
recipe.method: Follow the spine of the more extended nebula for radial extent, and measure mean vertical distance between upper and lower nebulae at disk edges for vertical extent. Perform Mann-Whitney U, Kolmogorov-Smirnov, and Pearson correlation tests across disk sizes, cos(i)-corrected fluxes, aspect ratios, and dynamical masses.
assumptions: 12CO emission and um-sized dust are much more optically thick than millimeter continuum; infinitely thin emitting layer assumed for cos(i) flux projection correction.

score_reason: All ALMA project codes, HST program IDs, CASA version, robust parameters, velocity channel widths, and multiscale scales are stated, and numeric results are thoroughly tabulated; however, visual/manual steps (channel selection, aperture tailoring, visual Keplerian curve fitting) and unstated uvtaper/self-cal parameters limit exact automated reproduction.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA datasets are public in the archive with explicit project codes, the analysis relies on standard CASA imaging, bettermoments, and 1D profile/PV diagram extraction, and full tables of fluxes, sizes, and dynamical masses provide a complete numeric answer key.
